QF.id: AIFM CII Investment Process and Governance_12

question.text: 'Vindhya Growth Category II AIF' holds a minority 25% stake in an investee company and negotiates a DRAG-ALONG right on the promoters. The primary purpose of this right is to:

answer.text: Force the promoters to sell their shares alongside the AIF on the same terms, so a potential buyer can acquire a control stake and pay a strategic premium
Prevent the promoters from ever selling their shares
Ensure the AIF receives 2x of its investment on exit
Give the AIF a veto over the company's dividend declaration

explanation.text: **The Logic:** Drag-along lets a minority investor 'drag' the promoters into a joint sale so the combined stake is large enough to command a control/strategic premium, avoiding the minority-discount trap. It's the key tool to ensure a minority AIF can exit at a fair valuation. **The Trap:** Drag doesn't prevent sale — it compels parallel sale. Veto on dividends is a protective provision. 2x recovery is liquidation preference. **Cross-Exam Context:** XIX-C tests this identically. For contrast, Cat III AIFs invest in listed securities so drag-along is largely irrelevant — XIX-E territory. **Manager's Pro-Tip:** Drag-along should have a MINIMUM price floor (say, higher of 2x of investment or agreed IRR) to prevent the AIF from 'dragging' founders into a fire-sale that damages reputation. Courts have set aside drags executed at distressed valuations.
